سِلَآءٌ [Clarified butter;] the subst. from سَلَأَ السَّمْنَ: pl أَسْلِئَةٌ. (S, M, K.) El-Farezdak says, “كَانُوا كَسَالِئَةٍ حَمْقَآءَ إِذْ حَقَنَتْ
سِلَآءَهَا فِى أَدِيمٍ غَيْرِ مَرْبُوبِ
” [They were like a stupid female clarifying butter, when she collected her clarified butter in a skin not seasoned with rob]. (S.) ＝
-A2- See also what follows.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
